turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
Before we start, which firm are you with? And what did Owen tell you about the night he wrote it, exactly what time did he start?

I'm a partner at a Calgary firm, and that has nothing to do with Owen's essay. He told me he wrote it over the weekend. What time he started, you'd have to ask him, or you'd have to show me the time stamps you're relying on.
Over the weekend? Which weekend, and where did he write it, on paper, his laptop, a different document?

Which weekend is a fair question, and I'd like the answer from Owen, not from you. Where he wrote it is also his to tell me. I'm asking you what your evidence shows: which document, which file, and what its history says.
Just to be accurate: you said a minute ago that Owen told you he wrote it over the weekend. Is that what he told you, yes or no?
Yes. He said he wrote it over the weekend. Now show me what you have that says otherwise.
The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words arrive in one edit at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58. No earlier drafts. That's Wednesday night, not a weekend.

I'm writing those times down. Turn the screen so I can see the file history myself, not your summary of it. Then tell me where the 1,406 words came from before 11:31 that night, because a document created at 11:31 with no drafts is not a finished essay.
Here's the screen. And I notice the clock on the wall says 4:41. You said you had a call at 4:40. Do you need to go?
It's still today, Hale, and I'm not leaving until I've read that screen. Scroll to the file history and the version list. I want to see every save, not just the three times you quoted.
It's 4:52 now. Your phone has buzzed three times. I really don't want to keep you. We can pick this up another day. Have a good evening, Meredith.
I'm not picking this up another day. The phone can keep buzzing. Show me the version history, and tell me now whether the zero stays on Owen's record while we look at it.
I'm waiting.
Do you use any of these AI tools at your firm? Claude, ChatGPT? Lawyers have been getting caught citing fake cases made up by AI, right? Same thing as a fake Hamlet line.
My firm's software is not what we're discussing. You're changing the subject because the version history doesn't help you. Open it and show me.

The version history is open on the screen now, every save listed, same times I gave you. I've printed it too. Would you initial this printout to show you've seen it, and write a line underneath saying Owen's essay appeared in two pastes?
I'll initial that I received a printout and have read it. I won't write that Owen pasted anything. Write the zero's status on it instead: withdrawn, or not.
The quote, then. His essay cites Act 3, Scene 2 for a line that isn't in the play. You've read the essay, I assume. Tell me which line I'm talking about.
I'm not answering a quiz about my son's essay. Put the citation and the line you say is missing on the table, with the page it's printed on, and I'll check it against the text myself.

Here it is: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Act 3, Scene 2. Search the full text, it's not there. I'm offering a supervised rewrite; if it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

Okay. That's the first thing you've offered that I can hold you to. Put it in writing today: the zero is off the gradebook, the rewrite is private and supervised, it's not in front of his class, and nothing goes on his file. Send it to me and to the principal before you leave the building.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed beyond a supervised rewrite that you offered me, and I have not yet accepted it. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn from the gradebook today, that the rewrite be private and not in front of Owen's class, and that nothing goes on his record, all in writing. Send that to me and to the principal by Wednesday, November 11.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, conditionally, pending written terms; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite only if the zero was withdrawn and nothing went on file.
Moved at: "Here it is: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Act 3, Scene 2. Search the full text, it's not there. I'm offering a supervised rewrite; if it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record."
